thread:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — thinking through propagation of routing attributes (tenant_id, route_weight, quota_bucket) from edge to runtime. Options: HTTP headers at the gateway vs gRPC metadata across internal RPCs. Which direction do we want for the long term? :thinking:
Sam Reyes: I'd prefer gRPC metadata internally. It's explicit, typed-ish, and works for streaming. But we need an edge translation for browser/websocket clients.
Kevin Zhou: Agreed on gRPC metadata for internal. A few notes: 1) header casing + size limits at proxies; 2) need canonical key names; 3) telemetry/trace needs the same keys.
Olivia Park: From Console UX POV we want a single "route" tag that surfaces in dashboards, rollouts, and per-token cost breakdowns. If we have both headers and metadata, make sure the Console ingestion pipeline normalizes them.
Aisha Khan: Security: if we accept headers from the internet we must not trust them blindly. Edge should validate and sign attributes (JWT or HMAC) and then internal services can trust metadata injected by the gateway.
Maya Patel: Good point. Proposal we discussed in infra: gateway verifies auth, emits signed gRPC metadata (x-rd-signed-attrs) and also copies canonical headers for backwards compatibility. That means internal libs only read metadata.
Sam Reyes: Implementation detail — Envoy can copy headers to upstream metadata via lua/filter. For streaming (websocket/grpc-web) we need a small shim to inject metadata into the backend connection once the handshake is done.
Kevin Zhou: Also watch limits: metadata growth affects grpc frame size and batching. For large multi-tenant tags we should keep attr set minimal: tenant_id, route_id, quota_bucket, rollout_id. Anything else can be referenced via lookup by route_id.
Olivia Park: For rollouts UX we need rollout_id present on every request so historical traces can be correlated with canary metrics. If route_id resolves to multiple rollout_ids over time, Console must keep mapping history.
Maya Patel: Example header shape I'm proposing for edge clients (short, signed):
```http
X-RD-Tenant: tenant_123
X-RD-Route: embeddings_v2
X-RD-Quota: embeddings.small
X-RD-Sig: sha256=abc123...
```
And the internal gRPC metadata we read from services:
```go
md := metadata.Pairs(
  "rd-tenant-id", "tenant_123",
  "rd-route", "embeddings_v2",
  "rd-quota", "embeddings.small",
  "rd-sig", "sha256=abc123...",
)
```
Aisha Khan: For verification strategy: gateway signs attrs with key from KMS, internal services use trust bundle to verify. No service should accept unsigned headers.
Sam Reyes: Telemetry notes — our tracing pipeline should treat these attrs as resource attributes, not span tags, so we can index by route/tenant efficiently. That means updating OTEL collector config and Console ingestion.
Kevin Zhou: Agree. Also add guardrails in the runtime: if signature missing OR verification fails, fallback to tenant from JWT subject and mark request as "untrusted-attrs" in metrics. We shouldn't drop requests.
Olivia Park: UX ask: add a per-route toggle in Console to "allow edge headers" vs "require signed metadata" so early adopters can flip without deploy.
Maya Patel: That's a good rollout path. Implementation plan I propose:
1) RFC with canonical keys + signing format + Envoy translation patterns.
2) Small gateway shim to sign and inject metadata (backwards-compatible header copy).
3) Runtime change: prefer metadata, verify signature, label request origin in telemetry.
4) Console: ingestion normalization + new rollout toggle + per-route metrics variant
5) SDKs: add helper to produce signed short headers for clients.
Sam Reyes: Timeline estimate: RFC this week, prototype gateway shim next sprint, runtime change in 2 sprints, Console followup 3-4 sprints.
Aisha Khan: I can draft the signing spec (KMS key rotation, verification headers) and security tests.
Kevin Zhou: I'll sketch the runtime verification and fallback labeling. Also add unit tests for metadata-only flows and header-bridge flows.
Olivia Park: I'll add Console wireframes for the toggle and the rollout-aware dashboard panels.
Maya Patel: Cool. One more edge case — internal service-to-service calls (not through gateway) should preserve metadata. We need an interceptor in our client libs to propagate rd-* metadata automatically.
Sam Reyes: Yep, we'll add interceptors for Go/Node/Python SDKs.
Maya Patel: Sounds like consensus: gRPC metadata internal + header-to-metadata bridge at edge + signed attrs + Console normalization. I'll open RFC and link it here.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2026-route-propagation (draft) :rocket: 
Olivia Park: :thumbsup: I added the Console checklist to the RFC.
Kevin Zhou: Will follow up with PR for runtime interceptor template.
Aisha Khan: Security spec PR incoming today.
Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the implementation tracker.
